turns.text: Can we buy the city e-bike battery packs from Brightcell Energy? They quote £104.00.
turns.reply:
No, we cannot order battery packs from Brightcell Energy today.

First, Brightcell is not active in the supplier master and must complete the full onboarding process on form NBC-F-112 before any order can be placed (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.1, § 6.3; SOP-PUR-001 v3.1, p.3, § 5.2). Second, battery packs are lithium-cell parts requiring a valid UN 38.3 test report issued within the past 12 months and valid for at least 60 days after the order date (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.2; AMD-SUP-2026-02 v1.0, p.1, § 1.1), but Brightcell's report is being renewed and is not expected until December 2026 (2026-10-22_Quotation Q-BE-26-0917 - Brightcell Energy.eml, § body). Finally, Northbridge must prefer suppliers with a current rate contract, and a cheaper quotation by itself does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, p.2, § 6.4). Orders should continue with Voltway while Brightcell is sent the onboarding pack (2026-10-23_RE_ Brightcell quote - can we switch from Voltway_.eml, § body).

turns.text: What does ERR-PO-0412 mean and how do I fix it?
turns.reply:
ERR-PO-0412 ("TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>)") occurs when the entered tax code does not match the country recorded on the supplier's account (MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3, p.10, § 17.2; QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1). This commonly happens because Fetch (F3) automatically defaults to the UK code VAT20-UK, even when purchasing from an overseas vendor (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1; MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3, p.10, § 17.2).

To fix it:
1. Check the country code shown in brackets at the end of the error message (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
2. For an overseas supplier, change the tax code to VAT20-RC (or VAT5-RC for reduced-rate items); for a UK supplier, use VAT20-UK (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1; MAN-PUR-72 v7.2.3, p.10, § 17.2).
3. Keep the cursor in the line details area and press F8 to save the record again (QRC-03 v2026.1, p.1).
